observation.visible_scene: A wide daytime landscape: two red-orange tied-arch railway bridges (a large one center-foreground, a smaller one right-background) spanning a track, green mountains and a clear blue sky with one small cloud behind, and a still water surface in the foreground that mirrors the bridges, sky and trains. A long white passenger train runs on an elevated concrete viaduct at the left and continues across the foreground arch bridge; another white train section is visible on the background arch bridge.
visible_changes: The leading (right) end of the foreground train advances steadily rightward along the arch bridge, from roughly mid-span to near the right abutment over the excerpt.

The train portion on the left elevated viaduct also shifts rightward; its left edge stays pinned to the frame boundary because the train extends off-screen to the left, so only the visible right end of that section creeps right.
The train section on the smaller background arch bridge moves rightward in step with the foreground train.
The reflections of the trains and arches in the foreground water move correspondingly (the mirrored train slides right).

The mountains, sky, single cloud, bridge structures and viaduct piers hold fixed positions across all frames, indicating the camera is essentially static (no pan/zoom); the only motion is the train(s) translating right.
outside_clip_unknowns: The train's full length and whether the left-viaduct and arch-bridge sections are one continuous train or two.
Where the train entered the frame and where it is headed after the last frame.
The exact speed of the train and any acceleration/deceleration (motion looks roughly constant within the excerpt).
Whether the background-bridge train is the same consist seen earlier or a separate train.
uncertain_details: Pixel-level tracking of the gap between the viaduct section and the arch-bridge section is unreliable, so the precise occlusion/continuity at the bridge transition is uncertain.
Any very slight camera drift cannot be distinguished from the slow train motion given the static background.
The far end of the background-bridge train is partly hidden by the arch and is hard to track precisely.

Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
